tables.name: peg_spells
tables.description: One row per peg spell (both definitions). Spells ending in exit/realign are breaks; chg_* = value change of the local currency 1-24 months after, vs anchor / USD / GBP (unhedged) / proxy (USD-hedged GBP investor shortfall). Negative = weaker.

tables.name: break_paths
tables.description: Monthly value index around each break, 100 = last pegged month, months -24..+36, one row per break and basis.

tables.name: regime_history
tables.description: IRR de facto fine classification as runs of months per country (1940-2019).

tables.name: episodes
tables.description: Curated breaks, near misses and edge cases: narrative, lessons and sources.

tables.name: episode_stats
tables.description: Measured moves per episode series: 'charted' is local per anchor as shown in the app; usd / gbp (unhedged) / proxy (USD-hedged GBP investor shortfall). Trading-day offsets for daily data, months for monthly.

tables.name: episode_evidence
tables.description: Dated evidence points (forward points, CDS, policy actions) with sources.

tables.name: episode_prices
tables.description: BIS rates around each episode (local per anchor). Yahoo-sourced series are excluded under Yahoo's terms.

tables.name: gcc_onshore
tables.description: BIS daily reference rates for GCC currencies since 2005, change points only (rate holds until the next date).

tables.name: gcc_offshore_summary
tables.description: Offshore-proxy deviation statistics (bp vs parity) and data-quality flags. Raw Yahoo prices not included.

tables.name: brent
tables.description: Brent crude, EIA Brent spot (DCOILBRENTEU) via the FRED® API.

tables.name: gulf_scorecard
tables.description: GCC scorecard as of 2026-09-14 (qualitative stress = this tool's synthesis).

tables.name: peg_screen
tables.description: Every peg still standing at the latest data, with drift inside its band, move since the 2019 reference level, peg age, and curated Gulf buffers.

tables.name: drift_signal_test
tables.description: Measured performance of the drift indicator: hit rate, false-alarm rate, noise-to-signal ratio and lead time.
